public_rationale: Tom's Hardware reported on September 21, 2026 that OpenAI forecast $278 billion in cumulative negative free cash flow for 2026–2030 [e1]. This is a projection for a different period, not a record of realized cash burn during 2025–2029 [e1]. It establishes neither survival through the 2029 endpoint nor the cumulative cash-flow result needed to assess the conditional forecast [e1].
limitations: The December 31, 2029 endpoint remains ahead of the evaluation date, and survival through it is unknown.
Complete, comparable realized cash-flow records for 2025–2029 are unavailable.
The contract interprets 'by 2029' as the end of that year; the phrase could also mean its beginning.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If OpenAI survives until 2029, it will have burned more than $290 billion by then.

statement.excerpt: There is simply no space in these projections to absorb that $300 billion, and from what I can tell, by 2029, OpenAI will have actually burned more than $290 billion, assuming that it survives that long, which I do not believe it will.

from_speaker: will have actually burned more than $290 billion
assuming that it survives that long
our_interpretation: Cash burn means cumulative negative free cash flow, consistent with the surrounding annual free-cash-flow discussion. It excludes fundraising, non-cash losses, and unspent contractual commitments.
The comparison period is calendar 2025 through 2029 because the surrounding projection table begins in 2025.
The latest reasonable deadline is December 31, 2029. The phrase could instead mean the beginning of 2029; that ambiguity does not affect the present assessment.
Survival means continuing to operate as OpenAI through the chosen endpoint.
The separate expression of disbelief in OpenAI's survival is not scored as an additional claim.
The accounting basis is estimate because Zitron builds his forecast from reported financial projections.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI survives through the endpoint and comparable realized cash-flow records show cumulative net cash burn exceeding USD 290 billion during calendar 2025–2029.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI survives through the endpoint and comparable complete cash-flow records show cumulative net cash burn of USD 290 billion or less during calendar 2025–2029.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Evidence that OpenAI continued operating through December 31, 2029, together with complete, comparable cash-flow records for calendar 2025–2029. Cumulative net cash burn above $290 billion would support the forecast; $290 billion or less would contradict it. Definitive cessation before the endpoint would mean the survival condition was not met.
